extraction_notes.note: The proof cites Lemma~\ref{lem:sum_sq_mod_two}, a label that does not exist in the blueprint, so no edge could be drawn for it.

The paper's macros (\btwo, \bthree, \Hstar, \opdim, \Gtwo, \Dbulk ...) are not defined in the source and stay unexpanded; constants such as N_gen, p_2, W, rank(E8), dim(K7), kappa_T and D_bulk are used throughout without any definition node to attach to.
The label thm:m_tau_m_e is used twice for two different statements of m_tau/m_e = 3477 (Chapters 6 and 19); both are kept as separate nodes.
Definition environments that state cited classical results (Bieberbach bound, Berger parallel-spinor counts) were retyped as external theorems.
A definition environment describing a procedure (PINN grid evaluation, FFT, rationalization) was retyped as algorithm.

Most 'theorems' are Lean-checked arithmetic identities without proofs in the blueprint; certificate theorems are conjunctions of the chapter's results, so their uses edges come from the chapter's results (inferred, not stated by \uses).

Chapter introductions that restate later environment results (e.g. the hierarchy formula, the Neumann eigenvalue identities, the K3 NK summary) and the proof-status table in Chapter 23 were not made nodes.

Near-identical results stated in two numbered environments (Pell equation 99^2-50*14^2=1; gcd(14,99)=1) differ in wording and commentary, so each environment kept its own node rather than being merged as a repeat.

differentia: derives Standard Model parameters from $\Eeight \times \Eeight$ gauge theory compactified on $\Gtwo$-holonomy manifolds
nodes.statement: GIFT (Geometric Information Field Theory) is a framework that derives Standard Model parameters from $\Eeight \times \Eeight$ gauge theory compactified on $\Gtwo$-holonomy manifolds.

nodes.name: Standard Euclidean Space
nodes.statement: Let $\R^8$ denote the 8-dimensional Euclidean space with standard inner product.
nodes.label: def:R8

nodes.name: Standard Basis
nodes.statement: The standard basis vectors $e_i$ for $i \in \{0, \ldots, 7\}$ satisfy $\ip{e_i}{e_j} = \delta_{ij}$.
nodes.label: def:stdBasis

nodes.name: Integer Coordinates
nodes.statement: A vector $v \in \R^8$ has \emph{all integer coordinates} if $v_i \in \Z$ for all $i$.
nodes.label: def:AllInteger

nodes.name: Half-Integer Coordinates
nodes.statement: A vector $v \in \R^8$ has \emph{all half-integer coordinates} if $v_i \in \Z + \frac{1}{2}$ for all $i$.
nodes.label: def:AllHalfInteger

nodes.name: Even Sum
nodes.statement: A vector $v$ has \emph{even sum} if $\sum_{i=0}^{7} v_i \in 2\Z$.
nodes.label: def:SumEven

nodes.name: E8 Lattice
nodes.statement: The $\Eeight$ lattice consists of all $v \in \R^8$ satisfying either: \begin{enumerate} \item All coordinates are integers with even sum, or \item All coordinates are half-integers with even sum \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: E8 lattice: vectors in R^8 with all-integer or all-half-integer coordinates and even coordinate sum.
nodes.label: def:E8_lattice

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Case analysis on integer/half-integer coordinates with parity arguments.
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis on integer vs half-integer coordinates with parity arguments.

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:sum_sq_mod_two}, sum of squared integers has same parity as sum. For half-integers, $\sum(n_i + 1/2)^2 = \sum n_i^2 + \sum n_i + 2$, which is even.
nodes.statement_short: Parity: sum of squared integers has the parity of the sum; direct expansion for half-integers.

nodes.name: Weyl Reflection
nodes.statement: For a root $\alpha$ with $\ip{\alpha}{\alpha} = 2$, the Weyl reflection is: \[ s_\alpha(v) = v - \ip{v}{\alpha} \cdot \alpha \]
nodes.label: def:E8_reflection

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Since $\ip{v}{\alpha} \in \Z$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:E8_inner_integral} and $\Eeight$ is closed under integer scaling and subtraction.
nodes.statement_short: Inner product integrality plus closure of the lattice under integer scaling and subtraction.

nodes.name: Fano Line Count

conclusions: The Fano plane has exactly 7 lines.

nodes.name: Epsilon Tensor
nodes.statement: The structure constants $\eps_{ijk}$ for the 7D cross product: \begin{itemize} \item $\eps_{ijk} = +1$ for $(i,j,k)$ a cyclic permutation of a Fano line \item $\eps_{ijk} = -1$ for anticyclic permutations \item $\eps_{ijk} = 0$ otherwise \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Structure constants of the 7D cross product: +1/-1 on (anti)cyclic Fano-line triples, 0 otherwise.
nodes.label: def:epsilon

nodes.name: 7D Cross Product
nodes.statement: For $u, v \in \R^7$, the cross product is: \[ (u \cross v)_k = \sum_{i,j} \eps_{ijk} \, u_i \, v_j \]
nodes.label: def:cross

nodes.name: Cross Product Bilinearity
nodes.statement: The cross product is bilinear: \begin{align} (au + v) \cross w &= a(u \cross w) + v \cross w \\ u \cross (av + w) &= a(u \cross v) + u \cross w \end{align}
conclusions: The cross product is bilinear: \begin{align} (au + v) \cross w &= a(u \cross w) + v \cross w \\ u \cross (av + w) &= a(u \cross v) + u \cross w \end{align}
nodes.label: thm:G2_cross_bilinear

nodes.name: Bilinearity in the first argument
nodes.statement: (au + v) \cross w &= a(u \cross w) + v \cross w

nodes.name: Bilinearity in the second argument
nodes.statement: u \cross (av + w) &= a(u \cross v) + u \cross w

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement_short: Antisymmetry of epsilon plus reindexing of the sum.

nodes.name: Coassociative 4-form
nodes.statement: The 7D correction to the Kronecker formula: \[ \psi_{ijlm} = \sum_k \eps_{ijk}\eps_{lmk} - (\delta_{il}\delta_{jm} - \delta_{im}\delta_{jl}) \]
nodes.statement_short: Coassociative 4-form psi: the deviation of the epsilon contraction from the Kronecker formula.
nodes.label: def:psi

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Antisymmetric tensor $\psi$ contracted with symmetric $u_i u_l$ vanishes.
nodes.statement_short: An antisymmetric tensor contracted with a symmetric one vanishes.

nodes.name: Lagrange Identity for the 7D Cross Product
nodes.label: thm:G2_cross_norm

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Expand $\|u \times v\|^2$ via coordinate sums. The $\varepsilon$-contraction decomposes into Kronecker deltas plus $\psi_{ijlm}$ terms. By antisymmetry of $\psi$ (verified for all 2401 cases), the $\psi$-terms vanish under symmetric contraction $u_i u_l v_j v_m$. The Kronecker terms yield $\|u\|^2 \|v\|^2 - \langle u,v \rangle^2$.
nodes.statement_short: Coordinate expansion; the epsilon contraction splits into Kronecker terms plus psi terms, which vanish by antisymmetry.

nodes.name: Scale Factor
nodes.statement: To achieve $\det(g) = 65/32$, we scale $\varphi_0$ by: \[ c = \left(\frac{65}{32}\right)^{1/14} \approx 1.0543 \]
nodes.label: def:scale_c

nodes.name: Scaling Derivation
nodes.statement: For $\varphi = c \cdot \varphi_0$ and metric $g_{ij} = \frac{1}{6}\sum_{k,l} \varphi_{ikl}\varphi_{jkl}$: \begin{enumerate} \item Standard $\varphi_0$ gives $g = I_7$, so $\det(g) = 1$ \item Scaling $\varphi \mapsto c \cdot \varphi$ gives $g \mapsto c^2 \cdot g$ \item Therefore $\det(g) \mapsto c^{14} \cdot \det(g)$ \item Setting $c^{14} = 65/32$ yields $\det(g) = 65/32$ \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Scaling phi by c scales g by c^2 and det(g) by c^14, so c^14 = 65/32 gives det(g) = 65/32.
conclusions: For $\varphi = c \cdot \varphi_0$ and metric $g_{ij} = \frac{1}{6}\sum_{k,l} \varphi_{ikl}\varphi_{jkl}$: \begin{enumerate} \item Standard $\varphi_0$ gives $g = I_7$, so $\det(g) = 1$ \item Scaling $\varphi \mapsto c \cdot \varphi$ gives $g \mapsto c^2 \cdot g$ \item Therefore $\det(g) \mapsto c^{14} \cdot \det(g)$ \item Setting $c^{14} = 65/32$ yields $\det(g) = 65/32$ \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: thm:scale_derivation

nodes.name: Scaled Identity Metric
nodes.statement: The induced metric is: \[ g = c^2 \cdot I_7 = \left(\frac{65}{32}\right)^{1/7} \cdot I_7 \approx 1.1115 \cdot I_7 \] Explicitly: \[ g_{ij} = \begin{cases} (65/32)^{1/7} & \text{if } i = j \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \]
conclusions: The induced metric is: \[ g = c^2 \cdot I_7 = \left(\frac{65}{32}\right)^{1/7} \cdot I_7 \approx 1.1115 \cdot I_7 \] Explicitly: \[ g_{ij} = \begin{cases} (65/32)^{1/7} & \text{if } i = j \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

nodes.name: Zero Torsion

nodes.name: Analytical G2 Metric
nodes.statement: The canonical GIFT G2 metric on $\Kseven$ is given by: \textbf{3-form} ($35$ components, $7$ non-zero): \[ \varphi_i = \begin{cases} +c & i \in \{0, 9, 14, 20\} \\ -c & i \in \{23, 27, 28\} \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \] where $c = (65/32)^{1/14}$. \textbf{Metric} ($7 \times 7$ diagonal): \[ g = (65/32)^{1/7} \cdot I_7 \] \textbf{Properties}: \begin{itemize} \item $\det(g) = 65/32$ (exact) \item $\|T\| = 0$ (torsion-free) \item $\mathrm{Hol}(g) = \Gtwo$ (by construction) \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: The GIFT G2 metric is the constant scaled standard 3-form with diagonal metric (65/32)^{1/7} I_7, torsion-free.
conclusions: The canonical GIFT G2 metric on $\Kseven$ is given by: \textbf{3-form} ($35$ components, $7$ non-zero): \[ \varphi_i = \begin{cases} +c & i \in \{0, 9, 14, 20\} \\ -c & i \in \{23, 27, 28\} \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \] where $c = (65/32)^{1/14}$. \textbf{Metric} ($7 \times 7$ diagonal): \[ g = (65/32)^{1/7} \cdot I_7 \] \textbf{Properties}: \begin{itemize} \item $\det(g) = 65/32$ (exact) \item $\|T\| = 0$ (torsion-free) \item $\mathrm{Hol}(g) = \Gtwo$ (by construction) \end{itemize}
nodes.label: thm:analytical_metric

nodes.name: Simplicity
nodes.statement: This is the \emph{simplest possible} G2 structure satisfying GIFT constraints. The solution is a constant 3-form with only 7 non-zero components and a diagonal metric. No PINN training or Fourier analysis is required---the standard G2 form is the answer.

nodes.name: G2 vs Fano
nodes.statement: The G2 3-form indices are \textbf{different} from Fano plane lines: \begin{align*} \text{G2 3-form:} &\quad (0,1,2), (0,3,4), (0,5,6), (1,3,5), (1,4,6), (2,3,6), (2,4,5) \\ \text{Fano lines:} &\quad (0,1,3), (1,2,4), (2,3,5), (3,4,6), (4,5,0), (5,6,1), (6,0,2) \end{align*} Both have 7 terms but represent different structures (3-form vs cross-product).
